cleared.result: x86_64: the binary is built for the x86-64 baseline and chooses code by CPU through the std_detect cache at 0x6cba970 (about 500 test sites) and through 120 cpuid sites of other crates. The evm2 jump destination dispatcher at 0x1e29620 tests bits 19, 23 and 27 (avx512f, avx512bw, avx512vbmi), then bit 15 (avx2), then bit 10 (sse4.1) of that word, which are the feature numbers of library/std_detect/src/detect/arch/x86.rs at rustc 0ef1bc386, and calls 0x1e29770, 0x1e29cf0 or 0x1e29fa0, or returns 0 for the scalar loop. The binary has no RUST_STD_DETECT_UNSTABLE override string. No ruint routine and no arithmetic handler reads the cache: ruint picks its x86 code (the div instruction for reciprocals) at compile time. aarch64: the NEON kernel is compiled in unconditionally (analysis/aarch64.rs line 19-20) and the ruint routines use the MG10 reciprocal table, with no run-time choice in either. So on the code paths this unit covers, only the x86_64 jump destination kernel depends on the validator's CPU.

cleared.result: Dispatch tables were read from the R_AARCH64_RELATIVE and R_X86_64_RELATIVE relocations: three handler families per binary (aarch64 tables 0x5da9a50, 0x5dc6098, 0x5dc6898; x86_64 0x6becbf8, 0x6c09a28, 0x6c09228). In both binaries ADD, MUL, SUB, the comparisons, AND, OR, XOR, NOT, BYTE, SHL, SHR, SAR and SIGNEXTEND are inlined into their handlers, so ruint's shift functions exist only inside them; EXP (wrapping_pow) is inlined in one family and called by the others; the ADDMOD fast path of modular.rs 37-49 is inlined in the handler (aarch64 0x3b5af74) and add_mod_by_ref is a separate function (aarch64 0x42b9334, x86 0x4af2910) that calls div_rem_bits_plus_one (aarch64 0x42b9448, x86 0x4af2a60) and rem_by_ref. MULMOD handlers all call mul_mod_by_ref (aarch64 0x42bab24, x86 0x4af3d90), with Product, the 2^256-1 end-around carry, rem_nxm_spare_limb and div_nxm inlined. DIV and SDIV call div_rem_by_ref (aarch64 0x18eceac, x86 0x19145b0), MOD and SMOD call rem_by_ref (aarch64 0x18eb894, x86 0x1913350), with div_nxn, div_n1xn, div_nxm, div_nx1, div_nx2 and the reciprocals inlined; submul_max stays separate (aarch64 0x28211b8). The aarch64 MG10 table (reciprocal.rs lines 85-103) appears once, at 0x1350fc4, and is read at 36 places in five functions: these four and a 512 bit div_rem. The x86 binary has no copy of it and computes reciprocals with div (reciprocal.rs line 30). The jump destination analysis is aarch64 0x1d47980 (analyze_neon, the only function with tbx) called from three identical copies of the lazy jump table builder (0x1d477c0, 0x32706b4, 0x4570a68) that inline analyze_scalar; x86 has the dispatcher and three kernels above, called from three identical copies (0x1e294c0, 0x3777260, 0x4e33560).

No validator hardware choice among x86_64 SSE4.1, AVX2, AVX-512 VBMI, no SIMD, or aarch64 changes a result. So no difference between validators of different hardware exists here for an ordinary account to use, and none of these paths gives a way to take or lock pool funds.

leadResults.answer: The x86_64 and aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu tempo v1.19.1 binaries (a9d6748, rustc 1.100.0, evm2 35aa328, ruint 1.21.1) were read without running them. Their jump destination kernels (NEON; SSE4.1, AVX2, AVX-512 VBMI and scalar), and every arithmetic, comparison and shift handler with the ruint routines they call, were lifted from their own disassembly into models and run: 70,031 jump table cases on aarch64 and 23,253 per x86 kernel, 826,464 aarch64 and 826,464 x86 handler runs, with no mismatch and with planted one-instruction faults caught, including the exact ruint 1.21.0 skip test. Statements now resting on the shipped binaries: cycle 10's L-612 and cycle 20's L-906 (NEON kernel; previously a software model of the source), cycle 18's L-582 (x86 kernels; previously a local rustc 1.97 build), cycle 10's aarch64 against x86 arithmetic check and cycle 20's L-879 (previously the x86 build with the fallback forced), and cycle 25's 21,537 vectors (previously the x86 endpoint only). Still resting on source or a local build: the reading of i256 signed division, the EXP gas rule, the handlers outside arithmetic, shifts and jumps, and anything about the aarch64-apple-darwin build. No release after v1.19.1 is published.
